fact: For natural a,r, the product (a+1)⋯(a+r) equals r!·binom(a+r,r). Consequently its quotient by r! in ℂ equals the natural-number (hence integer) binomial coefficient, including r=0.
justification: The probed theorem Nat.ascFactorial_eq_factorial_mul_choose states this identity for all natural a,r. The read recursive definition of ascFactorial is precisely the displayed product. Cast the finite identity into ℂ and divide by r!, which is nonzero because it is a product of positive integers (empty product 1). Apply with a=λ-i for X in its r≤i branch and a=i for Y in its i+r≤λ branch. This supplies only routine binomial normalization/integrality after the locally proved action iteration, not a new representation-theoretic step.

grounds.reason: For i∈I, 0≤i≤λ, so i and λ-i correspond to natural numbers.
X_r has r a nonnegative integer and divides by r!.
Y_r has the same nonnegative-index and factorial convention.
The action iteration displays the ascending products to normalize in both nonzero branches; all other matrix entries are zero.
